scenes.narration: The Indus people alloyed copper and tin to make bronze, which was stronger and more malleable than copper. There is no evidence that they used iron to make objects.

nodes: Pots painted red with black designs
props.label: Art and craft, p.31

scenes.narration: Two finely sculpted works of art came from Mohenjodaro: the bust of a bearded man and the famed dancing girl in bronze. Terracotta toys had moving parts, like bulls that could shake their heads.

nodes: Mouths of jars and sacks of grain sealed
props.label: Seals, p.31

scenes.narration: Most seals were square, made mainly of steatite, with animals and writing on top. They were pressed into soft clay to seal the mouths of jars and sacks of grain, for trade.

nodes: Uniform throughout the IVC: easier trade
props.label: Weights, p.31

scenes.narration: Cube-shaped stone weights in graduated sizes were found. The smallest is 0.856 grams, and the most common about 13.7 grams. They seem uniform throughout the IVC, which made trade between cities much easier.

hints: It gave the Bronze Age its name.
